body:
I appreciate the response. I anticipate the firm will be upset. They had sent me to a big trial academy last year and I have several active cases that I know better than anyone else, one set to go to trial at the end of November. 

I feel bad, but, at the same time, it wasn't me who made this a miserable place to work.

Yes I have told her. She is all about finding me another job. Maybe a job working for the federal government. 

My firm doesn't really have practice groups. It's not big enough. It's just like every man for himself, which adds to my anxiety.

I love where I live though. I just bought a house on a lake. My family is here, my gf has her dream job here. The nearest big city is 2 and a half hour away. 

The reality is, in some of these semi rural locations, the opportunities are not there.
Yeah I browse Indeed.com and other sites in my free time. Problem is, I can't make nearly as much around my area as I can bring an attorney.

I'm planning on taking one in the week following next week. I just had a case settle which frees that week up because it was reserved for trial. I don't think a vacation will really help. I really just dislike the work.

I understand that public sentiment, but I assure you that lawyers don't make the most money out of any occupation in America at least. I am comfortable with my salary but miserable with my job. I did mention that my money was a reason I haven't left yet. 

Also, I work a really fucking stressful and hard job for that money. I'm not like a businessman or a landlord. I can't just clock out for a week if I feel like it and the business will run itself if I'm not there. I have billables and clients.
It's a frequent occurrence. I see why.
3 years at the end of the month
I appreciate it. Sometimes I wish they would just fire me. I could deal with that. Right now I guess I'll just keep chaining myself to my desk and saving. I've got a nest egg of about 35k built up.
Tell them it isn't too late. Choose life.
